title: CHAPTER VI. Marilla Makes Up Her Mind
chineseTitle: 第 6 章：玛丽拉下定决心

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Spencer welcomed Marilla and Anne at her big yellow house in White Sands Cove. Mrs. Spencer expressed surprise and asked about their visit.
paragraphs.zh: 斯宾塞太太在白沙滩湾那所大黄色房子里迎接了玛丽拉和安妮。斯宾塞太太显得有些惊讶，询问她们来访的原因。

paragraphs.en: "Dear, dear," she said, "you're the last folks I was expecting today, but I'm glad to see you."
paragraphs.zh: “哎呀，真是出乎意料，”她说，“今天本不指望见到你这样的客人，不过能看到你我还是挺高兴的。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla explained they had come to correct a mistake. They had requested a boy from the asylum but received a girl instead.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉解释说，她们来这里是纠正一个错误。她们原本请求的是从收容所来的男孩，结果却收到了一个女孩。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Spencer confirmed that Nancy had told her Anne was wanted as a girl. Marilla admitted their fault for not coming in person.
paragraphs.zh: 斯宾塞太太确认说，南希告诉过她，安妮被当作女孩需要。玛丽拉承认她们本应亲自前来而没有这样做。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Spencer suggested keeping the girl, saying Mrs. Blewett needed help and could use Anne. Marilla remained unconvinced about Providence's role.
paragraphs.zh: 斯宾塞太太建议收留这个女孩，说布莱特太太需要帮忙，而安妮正好可以派上用场。不过玛丽拉对上帝的安排仍持怀疑态度。

paragraphs.en: Despite the unexpected turn of events, Marilla saw an opportunity to resolve the situation without feeling grateful.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管事态出乎意料，玛丽拉还是看到了一个解决问题的机会，并没有因此感到感激。

paragraphs.en: Marilla decided to confront Mrs. Peter Blewett about Anne. She felt uneasy about leaving Anne in her care. As they entered the cold, drafty parlor, Marilla and Mrs. Spencer discussed the matter with Mrs. Blewett.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉决定与彼得·布卢特太太谈谈安妮的事情。她对把安妮交给后者照顾感到不安。当她们走进那间冷清且透风的客厅时，玛丽拉和斯宾塞太太正与布卢特太太讨论这件事。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Spencer quickly pulled up the blinds and introduced them, then left to fetch buns from the oven. Anne sat silently on the ottoman, staring at Mrs. Blewett, who appeared sharp-faced and stern.
paragraphs.zh: 斯宾塞太太迅速拉上窗帘，作了介绍，然后便去烤箱里取糕点了。安妮默默地坐在脚踏凳上，盯着布莱特太太，只见她脸庞尖削，神情严肃。

paragraphs.en: "Are you eleven?" Mrs. Blewett asked bluntly.
paragraphs.zh: “你十一岁了吗？”布莱特太太直截了当地问道。

paragraphs.en: "Yes," Anne replied softly, her voice trembling slightly as she spoke her name.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”安妮轻声回答，说话时声音微微颤抖。

paragraphs.en: Marilla felt a mix of relief and concern when Mrs. Spencer returned, announcing that the Cuthberts wanted a boy instead of a girl. She suggested Anne might be suitable for Mrs. Blewett's care.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉在斯宾塞太太回来宣布库奇伯夫妇想要一个男孩而不是女孩时，感到一阵如释重负又有些担忧。她建议安妮或许适合由布卢埃特太太照顾。

paragraphs.en: Marilla looked at Anne and saw the child's pale face, filled with silent misery. This look made Marilla feel uneasy; she couldn't ignore it for long. Moreover, she didn't like Mrs. Blewett and was reluctant to hand over a sensitive child to her.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉看着安妮，见她苍白的小脸满是默默的哀伤。这一幕让玛丽拉感到不安，她无法长时间忽视这种感觉。此外，她对布卢埃特太太并不感冒，不愿意把这样一个敏感的孩子交给对方照顾。

paragraphs.en: "Maybe we should take her," Marilla said slowly. "Matthew is inclined to keep her. I just came to figure out the mistake.
paragraphs.zh: “或许我们应该收留她，”玛丽拉缓缓说道，“马修倒是倾向于留下她。我刚才只是想弄清楚其中的误会。”

paragraphs.en: Let's bring her home and discuss with Matthew first. If we decide not to keep her, we'll send her back tomorrow night. Otherwise, she’ll stay with us."
paragraphs.zh: 让我们先把安妮带回家，先和马修商量一下。如果决定不收留她，我们就明天晚上把她送回去；否则，她就留下来和我们一起住。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Blewett grudgingly agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 布卢埃特太太勉强答应了。

paragraphs.en: As Marilla spoke, Anne’s face brightened. Her despair faded into hope, and her eyes sparkled like morning stars. She leaped up and ran to Marilla when the other women left.
paragraphs.zh: 随着玛丽拉说话，安妮的脸色顿时开朗起来。她的绝望渐渐消散，取而代之的是希望，她的眼睛闪烁着晨星般的光芒。当其他妇女离开后，她一跃而起，跑到玛丽拉身边。

paragraphs.en: "Miss Cuthbert, did you really say I could stay at Green Gables?" Anne whispered excitedly. "Did you mean it?
paragraphs.zh: “库伯小姐，您真的说我可以住在绿山墙农舍吗？”安妮兴奋地低语道，“您是认真的吗？”

paragraphs.en: Or was that just a dream?"
paragraphs.zh: 或者那只是个梦？

paragraphs.en: Marilla sternly told Anne, "Learn to control your imagination and distinguish reality from fantasy." She added, "We might let Mrs. Blewett take you; she needs you more than I do."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉严肃地对安妮说：“学会控制你的想象力，分清现实与幻想。”她又补充道：“我们可以让布卢埃特太太带你去；对她来说，你比对我更重要。”

paragraphs.en: Anne passionately replied, "I'd rather go back to the asylum than live with her. She looks like a gimlet."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮热情地回答：“与其和她一起生活，我宁可回到疯人院。她的样子就像一根锥子。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla, despite wanting to smile, rebuked Anne: "A girl should be ashamed of such talk about a stranger." She instructed Anne to sit quietly and behave.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管玛丽拉很想微笑，但她还是责备起安妮来：“一个女孩不应该对陌生人说出这样的话而感到羞耻。”她命令安妮安静地坐下，好好表现。

paragraphs.en: Anne meekly returned to her seat, saying, "I'll do anything you want if you keep me."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮温顺地回到座位上，说道：“只要你别赶我走，我可以做任何事情。”

paragraphs.en: That evening, Matthew met them in the lane. Marilla had noticed his presence earlier and guessed his concern. When he saw Anne with them, relief showed on his face.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，马修在小路上遇到了他们。玛丽拉早些时候注意到了他的存在，并猜出了他的担忧。见到安妮也在其中，他脸上的忧虑顿时消散了。

paragraphs.en: They milked the cows together, and Marilla briefly shared their conversation with Mrs. Spencer.
paragraphs.zh: 她们一起挤完了牛奶，玛丽拉简短地向斯宾塞太太分享了他们的谈话内容。

paragraphs.en: Matthew said, "I wouldn't give a dog I like to that Blewett woman."
paragraphs.zh: 马修说：“我宁可把喜欢的狗送给布卢埃特那个女人。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla admitted, "I don't fancy her either, but we must take her or keep Anne ourselves." After much thought, she decided it was a duty. Though inexperienced in raising girls, Marilla vowed to do her best.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉承认：“我也不太喜欢她，但我们要么收下她，要么自己留着安妮。”经过深思熟虑后，她认为这是一项职责。尽管在养女方面缺乏经验，玛丽拉还是发誓尽力而为。

paragraphs.en: Matthew's face lit up as he said, "Well now, I reckoned you'd see it that way, Marilla. She is such an interesting little thing."
paragraphs.zh: 马修脸上露出了笑容，脱口而出：“玛丽拉，我想你一定会这么看的。她真是个有趣的小家伙。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla retorted, "If she's useful, that'll be more to the point." She vowed to train the girl accordingly but warned Matthew not to interfere with her methods. Marilla believed an old maid had more wisdom in raising a child than an old bachelor.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉反驳说：“如果她有用，那就更有意义了。”她决心按自己的方法来训练这个女孩，并警告马修不要干预她的做法。玛丽拉认为，一个老处女在抚养孩子方面比一个老单身汉有更多的智慧。

paragraphs.en: Matthew assured her, "You can have your way, Marilla. Just be kind without spoiling her. I think she's one you can win over if you get her to love you."
paragraphs.zh: 马修保证说：“玛丽拉，你可以如愿以偿。只要善良一些，别宠坏她就行。我觉得如果你能让她爱上你，她是有可能被你感化的。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla sniffed at Matthew’s opinions and walked to the dairy with the pails. She decided not to tell the girl she could stay that night, knowing it would keep her awake. Marilla reflected on the unexpected turn of events—she was adopting an orphan girl.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉嗅了嗅马修的意见，提着桶走向奶牛棚。她决定不告诉那女孩可以留宿一晚，因为她知道这只会让她辗转反侧。玛丽拉思绪万千，没想到会收养一个孤儿女孩，这一突如其来的变化让她颇感意外。

paragraphs.en: This was surprising enough, but even more so that Matthew, who always feared little girls, was behind it.
paragraphs.zh: 这已经够让人惊讶了，但更令人意外的是，一向害怕小女孩的马修竟然参与其中。
